BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.

Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.

Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). # Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Caveat:** I have only the Seller's summary positions and disclosure letter, not the full SPA clauses. Clause references are as the Seller cites them. Figures (AUD 3.6m/~30% revenue, AUD 3.2m Riverlark, AUD 420k bonuses, AUD 180k Ironquay, 1,240 records, AUD 330k Sandbar) are the Seller's statements and are unverified.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price, AUD 4,800,000, described as "key negotiated."
- **Buyer should want:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000 (starting position).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; counter at 25%.** The 20% figure is a fallback that requires Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft, and none has been given. Matching the number does not clear it.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only recovery above the basket.
- **Buyer should want:** De minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000; seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; counter at 5,000 / 50,000 tipping.** The Seller's structure would bar most recoverable claims.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months from Completion for general warranties. Also proposes that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer should want:** 24 months. 18 months needs Amelia Frost's written approval. No limitation should cross-apply to other regimes.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; counter at 24 months and delete the cross-application language.** The "all Claims" wording is a hidden general-regime override.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer should want:** Separate regime; 100% cap; at least six years; outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Administrative convenience is not a basis for collapsing a separate regime.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses (9.3, 12.8, 20.5) apply to "all Claims of any nature." No carve-out is shown in the summary.
- **Buyer should want:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. Non-waivable.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; insert carve-out.** The "any nature" wording would capture fraud claims unless expressly excluded. Confirm against the full clause text.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** Disclosure Letter 1.1 discloses the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012) as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026. 1.2 discloses the Accounts, statutory registers and public records.
- **Buyer should want:** Specific fair disclosure only. No whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; delete 1.1 and 1.2.** General disclosure would neutralise warranty claims on any document the Buyer has seen.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No Buyer claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (8.3).
- **Buyer should want:** Blanket exclusion deleted. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry. Never excuses title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; delete.** Combined with SPA-N-006, this would bar claims on nearly every disclosed issue, so the known matters need specific indemnities or conditions.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. Consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent (cl. 3/6.3). The Disclosure Letter (§2) states no final consent or evidence of conditions is included.
- **Buyer should want:** Effective consent and evidence that its conditions (DD-002 cl. 11.3) are satisfied before Completion. Not consent-on-delivery. Reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; make effective consent plus condition evidence a Completion condition.** The Seller's own letter confirms the consent is not yet obtained, and the customer is reported at ~30% of revenue.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** Approx. AUD 3.2m outstanding, to be addressed by a release provided after Completion (cl. 2/7). The Disclosure Letter (§3) states it is not repaid and no discharge is included.
- **Buyer should want:** Current payout figure; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases. A post-completion release only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; require payout letter and direct repayment at Completion.** A post-Completion release leaves the Buyer exposed to the lender's security.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420,000) are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. The Disclosure Letter (§5) says it does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.
- **Buyer should want:** Specific funds-flow line item or Seller funding, plus triggered on-costs. Must not be silently excluded.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; add a specific line item or Seller-funded mechanism and quantify on-costs.** "A matter for the Seller" is not a contractual mechanism. Do not estimate on-costs until confirmed.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate." The Disclosure Letter (§4) notes DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open. This is not bank verification, and DD-004 cl. 7.3 conditions transfer of Project Materials on payment.
- **Buyer should want:** Broadened indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; broaden the indemnity and require payment confirmation or confirmatory assignment.** The Seller's narrow scope leaves Project Materials title uncertain.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material" (cl. 4.6/Sch. 6).
- **Buyer should want:** Preserve logs, investigate, require updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- **Recommendation:** **Hold; require log preservation, investigation and regular updates.** Neither side's materiality characterisation is established. Whether to seek a specific indemnity is a decision for Amelia Frost (not in playbook).

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)
- **Seller:** Ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer should want:** Assessment only. No automatic debt classification or price deduction. The three renewals (AUD 110,000 each, DD-008/DD-011) should be read together for timing and scope.
- **Recommendation:** **Hold; assess contract terms (unavoidability, termination, accrual).** The "ordinary course" label is an assertion, not a finding.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Tax, IP and title all moved under the general regime.
- **Buyer should want:** Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories kept separate. No hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Consolidation is the mechanism that would dilute every other protection above.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
- **Buyer should want:** Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject DD-012 as sufficient.** Require independent searches (e.g., ASIC company extract, PPSR search, certified register, transfer forms, authority evidence).

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer should want:** Tax and IP terms remain open. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject "settled" characterisation; keep open.** Refer to tax and IP advisers before any position is taken.

---

### Cross-cutting points
1. **Knowledge bar plus general disclosure.** SPA-N-006 and SPA-N-007 together would bar claims on almost every disclosed issue (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, incident, Sandbar, Mossvale, office lease). Known matters need specific treatment (conditions, funds-flow items or specific indemnities) rather than warranty recovery.
2. **Items not in your list.** The Disclosure Letter also flags an office lease notification obligation (§7; landlord consent not stated) and a Mossvale assignment restriction (§9; consent not stated as required). Both need review.
3. **Seller characterisations.** "Key negotiated," "fair and balanced," "settled," "ordinary course," and "not expected to be material" are Seller assertions. None is cleared under playbook §0.4 / §6.3 without Buyer authority.
